scope: Scoped review of ten complete current native viewports for source-land control clipping and retained water appearance. Pixel checks cover both profiles and all five cases separately. Not a full art approval.
observations: Bohai and Japan control color ends at source land; inspected open sea remains the same appearance with the control layer on and off.
Caspian control color follows the inland water boundary and visible source islands remain land; water texture is retained in both inspected layouts.
Singapore and surrounding source islands remain separated by visible unpainted water.
Both complete overview layouts keep the normal HUD and source-clipped minimap; no screenshot was cropped or retouched.
All ten measured cases have zero maximum channel delta on the sampled unobstructed main-map and minimap water pixels; land samples still change.
remaining_visual_issues: Continental ground and overlapping influence/control layers still produce conspicuous polygon and triangle patches. Regional transitions and the combination of the two ownership layers need further refinement.
City, unit and label density is excessive around eastern China. Strategic zoom requires clearer aggregation and label priorities.
Source coastline angularity remains visible; the Caspian shoreline styling is less consistent than the exterior sea coast. No unsupported geography was added.
Location-specific ports, bridges and landmarks, complete unit animation cycles and physical Motorola X30 acceptance remain outstanding.
